To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

functional connectivity estimates can be obtained from task fMRI data, but that this is only possible for the ‘rest‐like connectivity’ and that the pre‐processing strategy has a significant effect on these estimates.
functional connectivity estimation is sensitive to pre‐processing and time course extraction strategies.

1) functional connectivity estimates are influenced by the pre‐processing strategy used, 2) functional connectivity estimates for task‐induced data are not comparable with functional connectivity estimates for resting state data, and 3) the within‐condition method is more appropriate than the rest‐like method for the estimation of task‐induced functional connectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the analysis and visualization of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data.
the analysis of the temporal structure of the brain activity during a task and during a resting condition, and with the comparison of these two states.
the problem of functional brain imaging and its applications in the field of cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychiatry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no clear evidence that any of the pre-processing methods is clearly better than the other ones in terms of the functional connectivity results, and that the choice of a pre-processing strategy is a matter of personal choice, and that the functional connectivity results will not change significantly with the choice of pre-processing strategy.
the rest‐like method provides a more reliable estimate of the functional connectivity between two regions of the brain.

the functional connectivity estimates depend on the pre‐processing and time course selection methods, and that the choice of the method depends on the research questions and the type of the fMRI data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
functional connectivity estimates depend on the pre‐processing strategy and the estimation method.
the rest‐like connectivity is a good measure for functional connectivity.
the rest‐like method provides the most accurate connectivity estimates for fMRI data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to estimate functional connectivity in fMRI data using either a rest‐like or within‐condition estimation method, but only the rest‐like method can be used for estimating functional connectivity in fNIRS data.
the choice of time course selection method has a large influence on the functional connectivity estimates and the choice of pre‐processing strategy is important.
the functional connectivity of brain networks can be reliably estimated from resting state fMRI data.
